From a modest family background, he worked in mining before establishing a successful steel business and investing its earnings in property. His illustrated stories later developed into a brand of figurines, themed bars and licensed concepts.

long_biography.plain_text:
Ashley Sutton turned a Bangkok factory into an imagined world so that staff who could not read his English-language stories could understand the objects they were making. Visitors began coming to watch, prompting him to add food and drink. Other property owners then commissioned him to design their interiors.

For The Iron Fairies in Bali, he chose timber to draw on local woodworkers' skills, departing from the steel-heavy interiors he had used elsewhere. The venue combines passages resembling mine tunnels with workshop materials and private seating areas conceived as furnaces. Handcrafted figures and butterflies occupy the spaces between its darker industrial surfaces.
